headline: Our navigation is not "unhandled" — it is three non-communicating CSS-class toggles (`cCurrent`, `panelStack`, `cWiz.step`) with **zero** browser-history integration: I re-verified 0 occurrences of `pushState`/`replaceState`/`popstate`/`hashchange` across app.js + index.html, and `closePanel()` (app.js:3367) still runs `panelStack=[]`, bound to ✕ (3315), Escape (3544) and the scrim (3543). Not one of those failures is caused by not using React — React ships no router at all; React Router does, and its route table is isomorphic to the descriptor registry we already specified in `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-24-navigation-model-design.md`. That spec is a genuinely good piece of work, still accurate against today's code (I re-checked: `openFrom` = 11 sites, `showPanel` = 77, ☰ and the AI hub both still do `closePanel(); setTimeout(...,60)`, the home dock still does a bare `window[fn]()`), and it is **approved-in-draft but unimplemented**. Build it in vanilla now: ~11-13 tasks (≈1.1 CP2) against ~38-57 tasks (≈4-5 CP2) for a React port that would deliver zero new user capability and would throw away the one thing that genuinely cannot survive it — the `tnode`/`restoreHe` post-render DOM-text-node-mutation i18n runtime for 23 languages.
recommendation:
**Vanilla routing layer now. React not for navigation, ever — React only later if the live/multi-device screens force it.** Sequence:

**Now, in order (the spec's own stages, ~11-13 tasks ≈ 1.1 CP2):**

1. **Answer the 3 waiver-gate questions in §12 of the nav spec first** (they are blocking and unanswered since 2026-07-24): the D5 `openTools` reinterpretation, whether Back-at-root leaves the app, and whether "close everything" survives as a gesture. ~0 tasks, one conversation. Do not start Stage 1 without them.

2. **Stage 1 = D4-A Option B (~2 tasks).** ✕/Escape/scrim → `panelBack()` instead of `closePanel()`; ☰/dock/AI-hub dispatch → `openFrom(self, fn)` instead of `closePanel(); setTimeout()`; wizard `returnTo`. Six surgical funnel edits. Immediately kills the daily pain (nested ✕ throwing you home; 0-of-58 launcher slots having a back button) and is a **strict subset** of the final contract — nothing is redone.

3. **Stage A = the NAV core (~4 tasks).** `{s, v, st}` in `history.state`; `NAV.render` the only DOM writer, `NAV.go/replace/commit` the only history writers, `popstate → render` and nothing else, `NAV._applying` re-entrancy guard; the 5 funnels (`showPanel`/`closePanel`/`panelBack`/`cNavGo`/`cwGo`) route through it; registry seeded with the single `__legacy` entry. **This alone delivers ~80% of the felt win** — hardware Back works, all four dismiss affordances mean "back one", screen + wizard step + catalog view survive a reload/backgrounding. That is 6 tasks total ≈ half a CP2, ≈ 12% of a React port.

4. **Stage B = descriptors + URLs (~3 tasks).** Register the 43 class-A/B/C surfaces (mostly one line each), `?nav=<encoded>` + `?item=cut-brisket`, the T15 `__legacy` census test **written RED in Stage A** as the exit gate.

5. **Stage C = the residue (~2-3 tasks).** Class D/E get `restore:'parent'`; the two prerequisite refactors (kill the `backFn` closure parameter in `openSeasonRecAI`, extract `openEquipment`'s function-local `editId` into a descriptor param); delete `openTools` (29 dead lines) and `openPantry`'s dead body (34 lines).

**One amendment to the spec, driven by the multi-device lens (do it inside Stage B, not after):** the route params must be drawn from the **same entity keyspace the sync layer will use**, not from view state. Event ids are already stable and URL-safe (`evGenId()` at app.js:9632 → `ev-<base36ts>-<rand>`), but `evScope()` (app.js:9627) also returns the non-entities `'cook'` and `'draft'`, and there is no event id anywhere in a route today. Make `?nav=` carry `{s:'events', v:{ev:'ev-a1b2'}, st:[{id:'timeline', p:{ev:'ev-a1b2'}}]}` so "open the same cook on the PC" is one URL. This makes **subsystem S4 (identity & scope keyspace, 6 gaps, `P5b` NOT STARTED)** a shared prerequisite of deep links *and* sync — design the id scheme once, not twice.

**Sequencing vs the approved CP2 work:** run Stage 1 + Stage A **after CP2 ships, before CP3**. Stage A touches only the 5 funnels plus a new NAV block; CP2 Tasks 3/5/7 are rewriting `openCut`'s panel body and its selection state machine. Doing both at once means two agents editing the same panel-render path. Stage B/C can then interleave with CP3/E4.

**When React becomes a real conversation — and it is not now:** when a second device pushing a live change into an open Timeline/Copilot screen makes hand-rolled DOM patching across 57 panels the bottleneck. Then port **that one screen** behind the NAV route boundary (the route registry is precisely the seam that makes a per-screen port possible) — not the app.

survives.asset: The navigation model design spec itself (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-24-navigation-model-design.md, 673 lines) + the audit behind it (docs/analysis/2026-07-24-navigation-model-audit.md)
survives.survivesHow: It is a router *route table*, not a vanilla implementation. The descriptor `{id, p:{...}}` with a stable id and JSON-only params maps 1:1 onto a React Router route path + params. The `restore: full|parent|none` classification of all 57 surfaces is a product decision about what may be rebuilt from data — it is framework-independent and would be re-derived identically for React Router loaders.
survives.condition: Keep descriptor ids stable-by-contract and deliberately NOT equal to the opener function name (§5.2 already says this). The moment an id is `openCut` instead of `cut`, it becomes a JS symbol and stops being portable.

survives.survivesHow: A URL is a public contract — shared links, PWA relaunch, the sync 'open this event on the PC' story. React Router consumes the same query string; only the parser moves.
survives.condition: Keep it a query parameter on the existing document (§3), not a path. `serve.js:42-45` 404s any non-`/index.html` path and Cloudflare Pages serves dist/ the same way — a path route needs an SPA `_redirects` rule that does not exist, and it would fall outside the warm-page fixture's `APP_DOC_RE = /\/index\.html($|\?)/` (tests/_fixtures.ts:67), silently re-introducing the loopback stall L22 exists to prevent.

survives.asset: `resolveItem(key)` + `_openItemByKey(key)` — 4 stable key namespaces (cut-/spec-/make-/umake-) already resolving the 279-recipe catalog
survives.survivesHow: The hardest part of any router design here — turning the catalog into addressable routes — is already built and already has a production consumer. Ports verbatim to React Router params.
Already stable, unique, URL-safe. Serves as the route param AND the sync primary key with no change.
survives.condition: Stop `evScope()` (app.js:9627) from conflating entity ids with the pseudo-scopes 'cook' and 'draft'. Those two must become explicit non-entity route states, or every route param becomes 'sometimes an id, sometimes a mode' — the exact ambiguity S4 (six gaps, four incompatible scope namespaces) already costs us.

survives.survivesHow: IF the tests navigate by URL (`goto('/index.html?nav=…')`, `goBack()`) and assert on rendered DOM, they survive a React port intact and become its safety net. This is the single highest-leverage conditional in this whole analysis.
survives.condition: Write every new nav test against the URL and the rendered DOM — NEVER via `page.evaluate('cNavGo(...)')`. Today 40 of 126 spec files navigate by calling app globals (openEquipment ×31, openTimeline ×23, closePanel ×18, cwGo ×11, cNavGo ×10, showPanel ×7); every one of those dies in a React port. Each spec migrated to URL navigation as NAV lands is one fewer casualty. Do NOT bulk-migrate them as a project — migrate opportunistically when a spec is touched anyway.

survives.asset: The two prerequisite refactors in Stage C
survives.survivesHow: Killing `openSeasonRecAI`'s `backFn` closure parameter and extracting `openEquipment`'s function-local `editId` (app.js, 5 showPanel sub-views with no external name) are exactly the refactors a React port would force on day one. Doing them under NAV means doing them once, with tests, at leisure.
survives.condition: Do them in Stage C rather than deferring — they are the two registration blockers named in §8, and deferring them is what leaves `__legacy` permanent.

survives.asset: All the HTML structure, CSS, RTL work, and the L(he,en) literals inside the panel templates
survives.survivesHow: A React port changes the *assembly* (template string + imperative listener wiring → JSX), not the markup or the styles. The L(he,en) call sites survive in JSX, so Guard A (coverage) and Guard D (call-site structural signature over `L(`/`t(`/`toast(`) keep working.
survives.condition: None — this is why a React port is expensive rather than impossible.

dies.asset: The entire i18n runtime application layer: `tnode` (app.js:8720), `restoreHe` (8738), `applyI18n` (8717), `hydrateMT` (8832), and the `_mkO` / `_mkHtml` / `_mko_<attr>` / `_mkMt` expandos
dies.whyLost: `tnode` walks the DOM *after* render with a TreeWalker and mutates `node.nodeValue` in place, stashing the Hebrew original on a `node._mkO` expando; `restoreHe` reads those expandos back. React owns its text nodes: it will either clobber the translation on re-render, or — worse — skip the write because its virtual value is unchanged, leaving a stale translation. The expando trick has already bitten us in the current architecture (app.js has a live comment: `cloneNode strips the i18n _mkO restore expando → title stuck in the other language`), which is the same class of failure React would make systemic. `showPanel` (3306) calls all three of `applyI18n`/`tnode`/`hydrateMT` on every panel open — the shell and the i18n layer are the same layer.
dies.couldWeSaveIt: Partly. The dictionaries, the extractor, Guard A/B/C/D and the L() literals survive. What dies is the *application mechanism* for 23 languages — it must be re-architected into the render path (translate at L()/component level, never post-hoc). That is 6-10 tasks and it is the single largest genuinely-thrown-away chunk in a React migration. **This is the concrete answer to `חבל על העבודה` — and note that building the vanilla NAV layer does not add one line to it.**

dies.asset: The imperative post-render listener wiring in all 57 panel surfaces
dies.whyLost: Every panel renders an innerHTML template string, then queries and wires its own listeners (`$('#panel').querySelectorAll('[data-mfn]').forEach(el => el.addEventListener(...))` in openMoreSheet, `[data-aifn]` in openAiHub, `[data-aptheme]/[data-apfont]/[data-apscale]` in openAppearance, and so on across 77 showPanel sites). None of it is mechanical to convert — it is per-panel bespoke.
dies.couldWeSaveIt: No. It is the bulk of the 20-30 tasks in a React port. Building NAV now neither adds to it nor reduces it — NAV changes *when* a panel opens, not *how* it renders.

dies.asset: 40 of 126 Playwright spec files' navigation calls
dies.whyLost: They drive the app by calling internal globals through `page.evaluate` — those globals cease to exist under React.
dies.couldWeSaveIt: Yes, and this is the actionable one: URL-based navigation in new tests saves them prospectively. See the condition on the test contract above.

dies.asset: `build.py`'s single-file inline pipeline as-is, and the warm-page fixture's byte-identity assumption
dies.whyLost: React needs a bundler. `vite-plugin-singlefile` can still emit one file so the product shape survives, but build.py's F5 single-definition module guards, the i18n Guard sequencing, `dist/sw.js`, `_headers` and the manifest all move, and the fixture's `route.fulfill(readFileSync('dist/index.html'))` + the certified `workers: 20` / ~54s suite timing must be re-measured from scratch.
dies.couldWeSaveIt: The F5 guard *concept* ports. The measured suite performance certification does not — it must be re-earned.

triggers: A user (or the owner) asks for a link they can send someone, or says 'open this cook on the laptop' — the route/entity model must exist BEFORE sync ships, or the id scheme gets designed twice and the second design has to migrate the first one's saved URLs.

The first report of a lost in-flight cook after backgrounding/rotation/reload at the smoker. Today reload always lands on home + catView('landing'): screen, panel and wizard step are all plain JS variables. Stage A alone fixes this. Do not wait for this trigger — it is the product's core use case.

Sync goes live while `wpck:<scope>:<translated label>` (app.js:7368) is still the work-plan checkbox key. Two devices set to different languages will silently diverge and collide their ticks. This is gap B13 (subsystem S4, OPEN) and it becomes a data-corruption bug the moment state crosses devices — fix it in the same S4 keyspace pass as the route params.

A second device pushes a live change into an OPEN Timeline or Copilot screen. This is the first genuine React trigger in the whole product: `openCopilot` already self-re-renders on every probe/target edit and `openTimeline` rebuilds its whole list, so server-pushed updates across 57 imperatively-wired panels is where vanilla actually breaks down. Port THAT screen behind the NAV route boundary — not the app.

app.js crosses ~15k lines (it is 11,564 today, up from 9,969 when the nav spec was written six days ago — that is ~1.6k lines/day of growth), or a second developer joins. Then the `registered-2026-07-25-appjs-modularization` roadmap's `NAV` module extraction stops being optional, and a framework conversation becomes legitimate.

Android hardware Back is verified on a physical device for the first time and behaves differently from Chromium desktop `goBack()`. Both the audit's §7 and the spec's §12 flag this as never having been tested on real hardware — it is the one assumption in the whole design with no evidence behind it.

risks.risk: **Rule N-1 (push vs replace) is implemented naively and every checkbox tick becomes a history entry.** Seven surfaces re-call their own opener on in-panel edits: `openRecipeShop` (×3), `openPantryShop`, `openProjectCart`, `openCart` (×2), `openBurgerBuilder`, `openCopilot`, `openPantry`. Under 'push on every showPanel', Back would walk the user backwards through their own checkbox states — strictly worse than today, and it lands on the shopping list the user is holding at the butcher.
risks.mitigation: The spec's Rule N-1 is normative: a `showPanel` whose descriptor equals the current top descriptor is a `replaceState`, not a push. Prove it with test T11 written RED: open recipe shopping, tick 5 checkboxes, assert `history.length` UNCHANGED, then one Back returns to the parent — not to checkbox #4. This is the highest-risk single rule in the layer; give it its own task.

risks.risk: **`__legacy` becomes permanent.** Stage A's unregistered-panel fallback is exactly the L2 / DoD-5 shape — an inert placeholder that quietly ships forever, leaving an app where some panels restore and some do not, which is more confusing than none restoring.
risks.mitigation: The census test T15 — sweep all 58 launcher slots, assert `__legacy` count === 0 — is written in Stage A **expected to fail**, and its going green is Stage B's exit condition. Not a to-do item: a committed red test. This is already in the spec; the risk is skipping it because Stage A ships and feels done.

risks.risk: **A shared/deep-linked URL names an entity the receiving device has not synced yet** (open `?nav={v:{ev:'ev-a1b2'}}` on the PC before sync lands, or after the event was deleted on the phone). The spec predates the sync conversation and has no answer for this.
risks.mitigation: Extend the §5.3 restore algorithm: an unresolvable entity param is treated as a `parent` restore — land on the events screen with the existing quiet toast rather than a blank shell. Add it as a T10 negative case now, while the restore walk is being written, not after sync ships.

risks.risk: **Re-entrancy loop between the dismiss affordances and `popstate`** (`popstate` → `closePanel` → `history.back()` → `popstate`…). Four affordances currently all call `closePanel()` directly.
risks.mitigation: The spec's one-writer discipline: `NAV.render` is the only function that touches the DOM and never touches history; every control calls `history.back()` and nothing else; one `NAV._applying` guard makes the legacy funnels no-ops mid-render. Plus T13 (Escape with `appConfirm` open closes the dialog and leaves `#panel.open`) — today the panel behind closes.

risks.risk: **Collision with CP2.** CP2 Tasks 3/5/7 rewrite `openCut`'s panel body, its selection state machine and its raw-data table; Stage A rewires `showPanel`/`closePanel`. Two agents in the same panel-render path in an 11.5k-line single file.
risks.mitigation: Sequence, don't parallelize: Stage 1 + Stage A after CP2 ships, before CP3. Stage A touches only the 5 funnels plus a new NAV block, so once CP2 is in, the overlap is nil.

risks.risk: **Back at the root leaves the app** — the platform-correct choice, but a mis-tap at the root closes an installed PWA mid-cook, with dirty hands, outdoors. And by the time `popstate` fires the history entry has already changed: a guard cannot cancel a hardware Back.
risks.mitigation: This is spec §12 item 2, still unanswered by the owner and hard to reverse once users learn it. Given the outdoor/dirty-hands reality I lean toward a confirm-toast at the root when a cook is live (`_liveCookState().live` already exists and already drives the home banner) and the bare platform convention otherwise. Owner decision — raise it in conversation, not in a document.

risks.risk: **Deciding React on navigation grounds and discovering it did not include a router.** React ships no navigation. The route table, the modal-stack-in-history model, the restore classes and the push/replace intent all still have to be designed — identically to what the spec already contains.
risks.mitigation: Name it out loud: our navigation failures are 100% attributable to having no history/route model and 0% to not using React. React Router would also model our panel stack *worse* than the spec does — its answer to modal stacks is the awkward `location.state` background-route pattern, whereas a stack array in `history.state` is a direct fit.

risks.risk: **Code-splitting-per-route is cited as a React win and then actually shipped.** For this product it is negative value: a user at a smoker on weak signal who taps a screen whose chunk never downloaded gets a dead screen mid-cook. The single-file 2.4 MB PWA is a deliberate reliability decision.
risks.mitigation: Treat route-level code splitting as an anti-goal regardless of framework. If bundle size ever becomes the problem, the answer is trimming DATA behind the authenticated proxy (04a-architecture §5), not lazy screens.

effort:
**Unit: CP2 = 11 tasks / ~150 code blocks.**

**A. Vanilla NAV layer — the recommended path: 11-13 tasks ≈ 1.0-1.2 CP2**
- Owner answers spec §12 items 1-3 (blocking): **0 tasks**, one conversation.
- Stage 1 (D4-A Option B): ✕/Esc/scrim → `panelBack()`; ☰ + dock + AI-hub dispatch → `openFrom`; wizard `returnTo`; tests T3/T5/T7. Six surgical funnel edits. **~2 tasks.**
- Stage A (NAV core): `{s,v,st}` state, `render`/`go`/`replace`/`commit`, `popstate`, `_applying` guard, 5 funnels rewired, `__legacy`, Rule N-1, tests T1/T2/T4/T9/T13/T14/T16 + T15 written RED. **~4 tasks** — Rule N-1 alone deserves one of them.
- Stage B (descriptors + URLs): register 43 class-A/B/C surfaces (mostly one line each), `?nav=` + `?item=`, entity-addressed params for sync, tests T10/T11, T15 goes green. **~3 tasks.**
- Stage C (residue): class D/E → `restore:'parent'`; the `backFn` and `editId` prerequisite refactors; delete `openTools` (29 lines) + `openPantry`'s dead body (34 lines); the `keep:` draft persistence; tests T12/T17. **~2-3 tasks.**

**The 80% checkpoint: Stage 1 + Stage A = ~6 tasks ≈ 0.55 CP2 ≈ 12% of a React port**, and it delivers hardware Back, all four dismiss affordances meaning "back one", back buttons on all three live launchers, and reload/backgrounding survival for screen + wizard step + catalog view. If effort has to be cut, cut Stage C, never Stage A.

**B. React port, honest, navigation-motivated: 38-57 tasks ≈ 3.5-5.2 CP2 — for zero new user-visible capability**
- Shell + 5 screens + cnav + panel host under React Router: **~4 tasks.**
- 57 panel surfaces → components (77 `showPanel` sites; every panel wires its own listeners imperatively after an innerHTML render; `openEquipment` alone is 5 sub-views over a function-local `editId`): **~20-30 tasks.** This is the bulk and it is not mechanical.
- i18n runtime re-architecture: `tnode`/`restoreHe`/`applyI18n`/`hydrateMT` + `_mkO` expandos → render-path translation, 23 languages, Guards A/B/C/D re-validated: **~6-10 tasks.**
- Build pipeline: `build.py` inline → bundler emitting a single file, F5 module guards, sw.js/manifest/`_headers`: **~2-3 tasks.**
- Test suite: 40 spec files' `page.evaluate` global calls, the warm-page `route.fulfill` fixture, re-certifying `workers: 20` and the ~54s runtime: **~6-10 tasks.**

**C. React later, AFTER the vanilla NAV layer lands: subtract ~4-6 tasks** from B (the route table, the URL contract, the restore classes, the two prerequisite refactors, and every URL-navigating test are already done) — and, more importantly, the port becomes **incremental per screen behind the route boundary** instead of a single cutover. That difference, not the 4-6 tasks, is the real answer to "אם התוצאה תהיה כתיבה מחדש חבל על העבודה": building NAV now is what converts a future React decision from a rewrite into a port.

**Where React would genuinely be better, screen by screen (all small, none urgent):** the **wizard** (`cwGo` + 6 `cwPaint*` repaints — real nested-route + form shape, but its state is already in `mk-menu` on every change, so the marginal win is modest); the **catalog** (`catView` re-renders the whole 279-item grid on every debounced keystroke, with an existing perf comment at app.js:2207 about expensive per-item validity checks re-running — memoization would help, though caching already did); and the **Timeline/Copilot** pair (self-re-rendering on every probe edit) — that last one is the only place where React is likely to become genuinely necessary, and only once a second device is pushing live updates into it. Preserved-subtree state and scroll restoration are NOT React wins here: `cNavGo`/`cwGo` currently do an unconditional `window.scrollTo(0,0)` (app.js:9004, 9036), and saving `scrollY` per history entry in `history.state` is ~15 lines of vanilla.
openQuestions: **Blocking, unanswered since 2026-07-24 (spec §12 items 1-3, §4 Waiver Gate).** (a) D5 reinterpretation: adopt `openTools`' back-affordance mechanism for all three live launchers and DELETE `openTools` — outcome-closer to D5-B than the approved D5-A. Its 15 labels are hard-coded Hebrew with no `L()`, so reviving its surface would regress shipped i18n on the highest-traffic screen. (b) Does Back at the root leave the app? (c) Does 'get me out of everything' survive as one gesture, or become three presses from 3-deep?

Do we want shareable `?item=cut-brisket` recipe links at all? It is the one link a user would ever send someone, but it is scope creep if the owner does not want the product linkable. Dropping it changes nothing else in the design.

Should the route carry `?ev=<id>` as a first-class friendly alias alongside `?nav=`, given that 'open the same event on the PC' is a named owner driver? The spec predates that requirement and only designed `?item=`.

Has Android hardware Back ever been observed on a physical device? Both the audit §7 and spec §12 flag it as unverified. It is the single load-bearing assumption with no evidence behind it, and it is the owner's #1 named navigation complaint.

Does the sync layer's conflict resolution (last-write-wins on `updatedAt`, per 04a-architecture §4) apply to navigation state? My position is a firm NO — the route is ephemeral per-device UI state and must never sync, or your phone would yank your laptop's screen. But the owner said 'realtime currency' and may mean something closer to session handoff ('continue on the other device'), which is a different and much smaller feature: one explicitly-tapped 'continue here' that consumes a `?nav=` URL. Worth settling before Stage B fixes the state shape.

`evScope()` returns `'cook'` and `'draft'` alongside real event ids. Do those become real entities with ids (cleanest for both routes and sync) or explicit non-entity route modes? This is subsystem S4 and it is P5b/NOT STARTED — it is a prerequisite for deep links AND for sync, so somebody has to own the decision before either ships.
